I had first powered up the locomotive at home and was aware of the excess power to weight ratio. If doable, a 2nd switch could have been added for slower wheel rotation which would have resulted in more enjoyment and less frustration for the child.

As designed, this very small locomotive puts out much too much torque for the number of cars and the curvature of the track. Perhaps a potentiometer within the cab could have been used to reduce the voltage from the battery to the powered wheels. Otherwise, a fun toy that must be handled with TLC. Having seen it in operation, I would recommend this for a 5 YO or older child.

Ever After High 2-in-1 Castle Playset This thing is much bigger than I thought it would be - it definitely fits the Ever After High dolls. It snaps together well and the versatility of being able to easily switch out the rooms is pretty clever. If I was a kid I would probably love this - but I think I'd want it to be more structure to it. It's more like a stage backdrop - but then I guess it is all about make believe anyhow so helps to spur the imagination. Would be neat if they could have figured out a way to make it fold up like a case - similar to the way the old Barbie Friend Ship (airplane) did. (You'll have to google it to see what I mean- had one of those when I was a kid and played with it for hours!) That would have made it super easy to store and put away.

I do really like the versatility, as I mentioned earlier. There aren't as many accessories to it as I would have thought, especially given the price for this plastic castle. The details in the design are neat - with the tree-like pieces holding up the second floor. The clips to hold the dolls into place is also a great touch so the girls can pose the dolls into their scenes. This is going to provide hours of fun for my niece who is a huge Ever After High fan.

text_fidelity_a:
Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House For this kit, you're paying for the convenience of having everything organized and already there. Also, for the "magical" experience you can provide for your child. If you do "Elf on a Shelf" or Santa Clause or anything similar, you'll probably love the added magical part of this kit. (We don't. We're all different and that's okay.) The parent has to be very involved. It's not a kit you just hand over to the child. (The parent portion is in a well sealed container to help keep the secret, since I imagine many parents will attempt to hand it straight over to the child. That was my plan before I realized what it was.) The child will have to do activities, and then the parent will secretly leave another activity in the fairy house. This is suppose to make the child believe the fairies left them a gift. (For example: The child is to craft 3 fairy bells and hang them around their room. Inside the fairy house, they'll place a stick, pebbles, and a leaf. They'll then spin the house and ring each bell to summon a fairy visit.)

The quality is similar to the various "Box of the Month" type subscriptions out there for kids. In my opinion, there's more in the wizard kit. There is the same amount of activities in both, but there's just not as much to do in this fairy kit. (It seems more stickers and easy crafts.) It's not high quality, but it's still nice enough. The crafts are something that could be put together with supplies from a dollar store. But, it's so convenient having everything in one place, especially for a disorganized person, like myself. Plus, there'd the "magical" experience provided for those that desire it.

Though the wizard kit that is similar to this one could work for boys and girls(and this one still could, if desired), this fairy kit is definitely targeted to girls. At the end, I couldn't help but feel sorry for all the little children doing these activities, hoping to see a fairy. While gifts are left, which are supposed to let the child know a fairy visited them, they'll never actually see one, unless the parent does something extra. We just did the crafts, since we don't do imaginary things as real. Without the added magical element, though, this kit just doesn't hold near as much value. If you're like us and don't do Santa and all, I'd recommend another kind of kit. If you do love the idea of pretending fairies are leaving gifts, this might be a blast for you and your child, as long as you don't think they'll be too disappointed that they never actually see a fairy. Overall, I found it a little disappointing, particularly considering the current price(which changes constantly).
text_fidelity_b: Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House

My four year old is having fun running him around in "line" mode, where his sensors follow a black lined path on a white background. When he reaches the end, he turns around and comes back.

Daddy is having a little more fun with "code" mode, which is too complex for the little one at this point. You program multiple commands into the remote, and then you send Botley out on a small adventure, around the obstacle course pieces that you can set up with material from the box. It's simple and easy for an adult, but for kids, it will teach computer programming basics, planning ahead, and thinking before you act.

The box comes with a variety of cones, bricks and blocks, as well as arms for Botley and cards that can help you measure how far he's going to move, and doubles as a wavy black line pattern on the reverse side if you want to use it. As it stands, the manual explains a few little tasks you can try, written in tiny font in as few pages as humanly possible. I want more from this.

Challengers Card Game | Strategy/Interactive Deck Management Game | Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 10+ | 1-8 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Z-Man Games For this game, you really need to know what you're getting.

This is a strategy deckbuilding game with a lot of silly, and a little stupid. And if you're OK with a lot of silly and a little stupid, you will probably love Challengers! if you have a even number of players.

In Challengers, you are deckbuilding in preparation for a game of War. Yes, that game of War where you mindlessly turn over cards and hope for high numbers, even knowing that there are a bunch of low numbers in your deck.

The only player choice is made during the deckbuilding phase, and then you get to sit back and watch the chaos.

And if you're OK with a chaotic game like this, where choices are limited and it's all down to luck, then you've found a winner with Challengers! If you think this sounds like a waste of time, then for you, it probably is. We had a few stand up and cheer come-from-behind moments and a lot of inglorious losses.

This is a great deckbuilding intro for kids, and for the grownups with the right tastes, this will be a hit, but I think a lot of people will absolutely hate it also.
text_fidelity_b: Challengers Card Game | Strategy/Interactive Deck Management Game | Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 10+ | 1-8 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Z-Man Games

Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets This word game is for 3 – 5 players. It’s for ages 10 and up. Takes 30-minutes to play.

It comes in a cardboard box measuring just under 10” X 6.25” X 2.25”. It’s part of the United States Playing Card company, which makes Bicycle playing cards. Made in China.

Each player receives chips, totaling 30-points, to start. You also receive two cards. From there you go around and each person “pays” for additional cards. Cards with letters which are worth more. . . cost more. You go around four-times. At the end, everyone turns-over their cards and you have thirty-seconds to spell a word with the most points. Please Note: Timer not included. Whomever wins that round gets chips equaling the number of points for their winning word. Then the second place person receives chips worth their number and so on. After playing three times, the person with the most points wins.

FYI. . . This came was originally going to be called “The World Series of AlphaBets”. . . but somewhere along the way they changed it to “Fumbling Ferrets”, probably to make it sound more “family friendly”. But it has nothing to do with ferrets.

If you like word / spelling games, then this one is fairly easy and fast to play. If you’re playing with younger kids, especially to start, you may wish to extend the timer to come-up with a word by a little bit and then shorten it with each round.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets

text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.
text_fidelity_b: Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up

Dromida Ominus Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Quadcopter Ready-to-Fly (RTF) Drone with Radio System, Batteries and USB Charger (Yellow) Looks great, but it frustrating to fly. The Dromida Ominus UAV Quadcopter RTF looks like a 22nd Century, sexy military machine.

The battery for the copter charged quickly. The batteries for the controls come with, but you'll need a tiny screwdriver to get them in.

Flying inside is easier than outside, though completely not recommended. The copter is so light, it is susceptible to the gentlest wind. The controls are very hair-sensitive, making it difficult to steer with any accuracy. As such, fly in a large field. Otherwise, expect it stuck in a tree, land on a roof, or be busted up on the street.

Extra blades are included. After a few crashes, I can see they'll be necessary. I don't expect it to be durable with any extended use.

I'm giving it three stars because it does work as advertised. Overall, however, I'm unimpressed.

Picasso Toys Magnetic Drawing Board 12x10 inch Large 748 Bead Magnet Tablet Pad Erasable Reusable Writing Playboard STEM Toys Educational Playset Open-Ended Learning Kit Child Brain Development PTB01 In concept, great. I do think, if used as intended, it helps work their prancer grip muscles, which need to be built up in preparation for writing. Unfortunately, either the size of the letters are too small and/or the size of the magnetic balls are too big, because when you run the 'pen' over the letters, they don't pull up the balls in the way/order they should (some balls that I want to pull up later come up already, and some of the balls fall back down). Also because of how large the balls are, it is difficult to actually 'draw' something recognizable on the flip side.

I thought my kids (3 and 5) would love this product, and that it would help them identify and write letters. They do like to pull up the balls with the magnetic pull of the pen (science, so that's good), and push them back down with their fingers, but after two minutes they lose patience and are shaking the board. Be warned this is not the best tool for learning to write letters.. there are much better and more satisfying ways children can learn that skill.

The game includes a set of cards and a game board with different types of activities. As players mover around the board, trying to be the first to get to the end, they ask and answer a series of questions that tests how well they know those they’re playing with. There are yes/no questions, short answer questions, and some that require a little acting skill. It’s fun and full of laughs. For 3-6 players, 8 years and up, though younger kids can play provided they can read and write or play with a partner. The only thing I’m wondering about is whether there are going to be enough cards for the game to be fun for a long time? The body composition also has a difference over the American Girl or Playtime by Eimmie dolls. There’s a neck joint and the neck, shoulder, and upper torso area is plastic while the lower torso is cloth. Her clothing is designed with play in mind, making it easy for an older child to take on and off, but the quality is such that she would make an excellent addition to a collector’s display as well.

text_fidelity_a:
Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:58af1484fac2632df11b3d8e403acedc]] Addendum: Two years old now and these toys are still working great and popular with the kids. I assume the ease of filling in the pool and the ability to shoot whatever they want without getting fussed at adds to their appeal.

I got both the Matchbox Aqua Cannon Swamp Blaster and this Fire Truck Rig for 5 and 6 year old grandkids. Until I showed them how to use the toys, they didn't show much interest in them. Once the trucks were filled and squirting, however, they happily shot at their sister for about 15 minutes. It didn't keep their interest long but there were enough kids to share the toys that they stayed in action for an hour or so.

They toys fill easily and are easy to load and shoot. We submerged the trucks in the pool so that they self-filled meaning that only the kids were only limited by their ability to keep pumping (see photo).

I find these a great alternative to water guns. The volume and strength of the shots are less than those oversized guns but enough to shoot all the way across the pool. Because they are not guns, the kids are less likely to feel the need to aim them at people.

I think these toys are best suited for ages five and under.

1 year followup: This toy spent the winter outside by the pool and it still works like new. I have to keep it out of the hands of adults who delight in shooting water far outside the pool area (violating house rules).
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) Mattel has brought a new world to target practice and just plain fun with soft dart guns with this BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster. With no batteries required, the fun is endless. Instead of batteries to power the gun, it is air powered. You have to pump the gun to get enough air pressure to fire the soft darts. Mattel states the gun is for ages 6 and up, but this gun is on the heavy side and requires a bit of strength just to pump it, so I feel ages 7 and up would be a better fit. Even though our 6 year old neighbor didn't want to put this gun down, it was difficult for him to pump it for firing.

The gun is very sturdy being large and made of a heavy plastic. I can see this gun lasting quite a bit of use and not ending up in the trash for a long while. Once pumped it is easy to fire, whether firing one dart or the entire 20 dart clip. At the end of the gun is a special shield you can open up to not only protect yourself from oncoming darts, but your opponents darts will actually stick to this protective shield, allowing you to capture his darts.

Besides the gun there are 30 Smart Stick darts, a 20 dart clip and a Smart Stick target included. The target is great for improving your aim, especially firing one dart at a time. The 20 dart clip is really fun, whether firing at the target or your opponent, as it fires all 20 darts in a matter of a few seconds. It literally fires up to 50 feet, as we shot all 20 darts and several darts went well over 45 feet away. The rapid fire at such a distance is really a lot of fun for the backyard.

Even though these darts are really soft plastic, you will find out that once the children find out how much fun it is to shoot darts at both the target and each other, you may want to purchase the safety eye gear. I don't know if having all 20 darts coming at you from 50 feet away would need some type of eye protection, but I feel it's better to have some type of eye gear on. There is no doubt, this is a safe, sturdy toy with your children wanting to run around and play with this outdoors, gives it 5 Stars. Just getting the kids off the couch away from video games makes it a 5 Star toy, as the exercise alone is worth 5 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain My boys(3, 5, and 7) had fun with this kit, overall, but there's really not much to it.

Basically, you mix up cornstarch, gelatin(both provided), and water, through various steps, and then pour it into the provided molds. This project has to be done in several steps, with waiting periods in between. With my children being so young, the wait was annoying. Thankfully, we did the project on a day that it was beautiful outside, and there was plenty of play in between, so it could have been worse.

After the brain/eye has set up in the mold, you'll dump it out, and paint it. You get paint(food coloring) in the kit, and can mix it up to what colors you want. My children were disappointed that they couldn't get the colors to look as bright as they do in the pictures. I even helped with this attempt. The colors were just very dull, and our brain didn't look anywhere near how bright it was shown to be. I'd recommend using real paint, as opposed to food coloring. I think the results will be better.

The molds are reusable, so as long as you don't mind buying more gelatin and cornstarch, you can make as many brains and eye balls as you'd like.

Overall, this is a fun little experiment if you're studying brains or eyes. It's very simple, though, despite the several steps, which make it time consuming.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain

I am in my 20's and have only recently been introduced to deck building games, and instantly fell in love.
DOminion and the DC Comic deck games are my favorite, but Dominion provides a larger variety because the cards used change.
The game its self comes with several possible versions of the game.
For example, the game is plaid with several action card decks to draw from, but Dominion comes with twice as many action cards. So, no game is exactly alike. The rule book comes with various options of which action cards to play with for certain kinds of games.
This game is dynamic!

I first played Dominion at a bar with board games. After a few times I fell in love and bought this second edition. The cards are beautiful, more colorful than the first edition. (I attached some photos to see to see the cards)

It says that the game can be played in about 30 minutes... for me it takes closer to an hour with 3 players. It also probably depends on what type of game you play (which actions cards to choose to play with) But because we are still learning, maybe we go a little slower, constantly re reading what the action cards say/do.

At the end of the game, who ever has the most victory points wins.

text_fidelity_a:
Bgraamiens Puzzle-Blooming Color-1000 Pieces Color Challenge Blue Board Round Jigsaw Puzzles I just completed this puzzle, and have some pro's and con's to share:

Pro's: It's very pretty and big.
Pieces are appropriately thick for a 1,000 piece puzzle
Pieces are printed on the back with "A", "B", "C", "D". If you sort by letter, you will have all the pieces to do
1/4 of the puzzle. Great idea if your table space is limited, or if more than one person is working on it.
If you want greater difficulty, don't look at the back!
Storage box is good quality cardboard.

Con's: About 20% of the pieces were not cut through, so I had to tear them apart, causing damage to some of
the backs.
One piece was missing, and there was an extra edge piece. Based on other reviews, I won't bother trying
to contact the seller because no one else has had success doing so.

Overall, it was a fun puzzle to work on, despite the missing piece. I purchased another puzzle from the same manufacturer, but haven't put it together yet. If I have the same problems of uncut and missing pieces, I won't purchase anymore and certainly won't give one as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: Bgraamiens Puzzle-Blooming Color-1000 Pieces Color Challenge Blue Board Round Jigsaw Puzzles

text_fidelity_a:
Kanagawa Game Kanagawa is a board game about making the most cohesive panorama painting.

The first thing you'll notice about Kanagawa is that it has tremendous components. The little paintbrush bits are unique and well-made, and the way that the cards fit together is really cool. The art and graphic design make it easy for players to figure out how to play, and even the board is well-designed.

Unfortunately, gameplay is pretty basic. Each turn, new cards will be put on the board, either face up or face down depending on the positioning. Players can then either take some of the cards, or allow more to come out, opening up the opportunity to their opponents to take the "best" cards. You then place these cards in panorama fashion on your piece of art, or you can use them as "skill" cards to allow you to paint more interesting paintings on later turns. There are bonus cards, and opportunities to gather more items, but that's really about it.

Aside from the excellent artwork, the only other good thing about this game is that you can explain the rules in only a few minutes. Decisions that you make along the way really are not all that important along the way. You can collect a lot of abilities along the way that you never get the opportunity to use, or you can find that you'd rather not use them because there are better moves for you. Overall, this game was pretty fast, easy to learn, but felt like your decisions were pretty arbitrary, and didn't matter in the end.
text_fidelity_b: Kanagawa Game

text_fidelity_a:
Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women I could not tell exactly how these “puzzles” work, even after looking at the video. You have to do two different things. First you have to “flip” each of the circles back-and-forth until you get all of them flipped to the correct side. Then you have to “spin” each of the circles to align them correctly. I find that it’s best to start from the outside circle and work your way in. The “puzzles” with most similar colors / designs on each side are the most challenging to work to get the circles on the correct side.

FYI. . . Once you have completed one side, the opposite side will not be complete. So though you will not have to flip the circles. . You’ll have to rotate the circles to complete the puzzle. So you’ll always have one side complete, and one size incomplete.

It should be noted that this “puzzle” is sturdy enough for a puzzle such as this, but it can certainly be pulled apart and broken without too much effort.

I think this “puzzle” to be best for ages tweens and up. It’s not super challenging, but again the ones with the common colors on both sides are the most challenging.

This puzzle is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Aroma Putty, Silly Putty Alternative, Gift, 4 Count I am so glad I waited a few weeks to review this product -- When it first arrived, my reactions was little more than, "Hmm, that's interesting." I had the hardest time figuring out how to open the containers (they twist open), and the first few I opened had a very chemically, medicinal, almost artificial scent. Plus, I no longer subscribe to a daily newspaper, so the silly putty fun of my childhood -- copying pictures from the funny pages onto the putty -- was not really an option. Meh. It's okay. Kind of novel but not particularly useful.

I was headed to a funeral the next day, and I brought one of these along, thinking it might be a harmless diversion if I needed a little stress relief. I started with the peppermint. It smelled nice enough. Minty, a little bit chemical, but nice. Then I started to play with it, kneading it in my hand. At first, it was pretty hard, and I had to dig it out of the container. In no time, it became softer, just the right texture for kneading, stretching, twisting, wrapping around my finger, collapsing, kneading. It was kind of fun. I put it back in the container. My daughter opened each of the containers, stamping designs into the putty. The designs remained until the next time I opened the containers.

Since the funeral, I have had several IVs and blood draws. I brought along a little container of putty to the hospital, and found it worked just perfectly for the "make a fist and squeeze" stage. It was fun and distracting to play with while the IV was going. I keep a container in my purse, and find it fun to play with while riding the bus or subway, and when I need a whiff of something pleasant (as can happen when taking public transportation), I just hold the putty up to my nose. I can smell it, but the smell is not so strong or overwhelming as to bother others sitting nearby. And, as my husband discovered when he found a local high school newspaper, you can still copy comics from newsprint.

The containers are small and easily slip into a purse or backpack. So far, I haven't had any issues with the lids coming off when I don't want them to -- which often happens to things in my crowded purse. Occasionally, the putty becomes a little too warm and starts sticking to things. I was vigorously kneading it for some time and the putty started to stick under my rings. When that happened, I just put it away -- and it was back to its original texture in short course.

Overall, I'm really glad I discovered these little treats. They are an adult alternative to fidget spinners, and have provided more hours of -- I'm not sure if I'd call it pleasure or relief or what -- let's just say they have been used for many more hours than I ever expected I would use them, and the seem to be holding up well, staying good as new.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Aroma Putty, Silly Putty Alternative, Gift, 4 Count

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. Okay, so I got the kit and made the TWO potholders. I bought this kit because the loom was metal, and I'd read reviews and seen videos where the person's PLASTIC loom would break. So, what's the problem?
I really don't like how the loops slip off this loom, especially when you're getting towards completing the project. Pop, pop, pop go the loops - OFF the loom! This might be the nature of pot-holder looming, but I think the problem is the little spokes (hooks) are straight, so there's nothing to keep the loops from slipping off. They should be curved and WIDER at the top so the loops can't slide off. Towards the end, when you're crocheting the edges together, the last side can get completely unraveled.
THAT IS frustrating.
I'm going to try to find another loom.
Unfortunately, I looked at a lot looms before I bought this one, and they ALL seem to have the same design flaw.

Afterthought:
On a positive note: the loops are NOT polyester, but cotton, so the potholders came out nice 'n thick and heavy.
I can see why posters said they lasted a long time. They probably will.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

Just watch they don't try to eat the batteries, I guess. It's not super fast, either, so older kids might get bored.

Anyway, they totally cheaped out on the battery setup. 400mAh?!?! Are you kidding me? Even the cheap, "included" versions of decent brands are 1100mAh, with good ones getting 2500mAh or more. And why the goofy charging setup? You have to take it out and then hook it to an oddball USB cable (so now you can't just use any USB cable you have laying around, you have to have this one on hand). They should just wire a higher capacity battery inside and add a micro-USB port like everybody else. And maybe similar functionality for the controller, which, oddly, uses two batteries...more than the car itself.

Pretty fun. Not well thought out overall, but on the other hand, if your kids falls out of love with toys quickly, maybe it's better not to spend more for the battery setup that could have been...

When we opened up the package, we had a couple of issues with the wood being cracked.  The overall setup is fairly easy if you follow the directions.  Customer service was really great working with when I called to get replacement parts.  To be clear, though, I wasn't aware that we'd have to seal the playhouse.  I only found that out because I'd called for replacement parts.  We used a marine sealant and it is full waterproofing!  We used a chemical pump sprayer to apply it (we sprayed it on and then brushed over it - it is very runny like milk and goes on white but dries clear).  I, originally, expected the wood to be pre-sealed since it was a playhouse specifically for outside.  So, in hindsight, I am very grateful that we talked with the helpful customer service person.  Otherwise, we'd probably have to be replacing the house next year ... and, I wouldn't have been very happy with the purchase.  However, we've had it a couple months now and it still looks brand new!  I'd highly recommend this playhouse IF you are willing to seal it.  Yes, marine clear coat is expensive but so was the playhouse.  All in all, a great addition to our backyard and I'm sure we'll get several years of grandchildren's fun with it!

text_fidelity_a: Air Hogs - Supernova, Gravity Defying Hand-Controlled Flying Orb, for Ages 8 and Up Still learning!!  This has had our house in a happy uproar since we got it!  After multiple readings of directions and many try outs we think we kind of have a handle on the basics but doing any tricks are an accidental result only.  Batteries are already in this.  Everything for power is concentrated in the center of this orb.  It comes w/USB to charge through our computer.  There is a tiny, tiny white slide tab in center by batteries that you move to turn this on.  Immediately (if charged) the center ball light will come on and flash colors.  When charging or a problem, the ball light will flash red only.  This is a fairly fragile  plastic caged flyer.  It doesn't weigh a lot because it has to keep it's self flying + hovering with 4 little sets of plastic blades that rotate (think fan blades).  Four extra blades come with this. Inside the orb besides the power center and the blades are sensors that will cause the orb to change directions when they are blocked in any way. To start, you have it on and slowly let it drop out of yr hands, it will drop and start hovering before it actually hits the floor(the sensors realize there is something in the way). After it starts hovering low over floor you get a hand(s) underneath and just start raising it and moving it all over the place by using yr hands to block the sensors...All the while, center light is flashing colors and the orb is making this noise..lol, between a whine & buzz and you find yrself almost running around the room trying to control this thing!  It will go up to the ceiling and then you have to figure out how to get a hand up to control it!  We don't dare take it outside to do, afraid it wouldn't come back!  This has fallen to the floor several times and not broken but, it is something you should take care with.  A lot of great accidental exercise and laughs!  Not for little children to use but they will love the show
text_fidelity_b: Air Hogs - Supernova, Gravity Defying Hand-Controlled Flying Orb, for Ages 8 and Up
